title: Processing of identified data during account registration
description: Homeowner provides personally identifiable information (name, email, etc.) during account registration, which is processed by the system.

title: Excessive data type sensitivity during device enrollment
description: During camera/sensor enrollment, the system may collect more sensitive data types than functionally required for the registration process.

title: Identifiers in data flow during registration
description: Account identifiers and device identifiers are transmitted during the registration flow, potentially exposing identifiable information in transit.

title: Home Hub collects excessive data types
description: The Home Hub process may collect more sensitive personal data than functionally required for account registration and device enrollment.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and enrichment
description: The Home Hub may process, analyze, or enrich the registration data beyond what is necessary for the functional goal of account creation and device enrollment.

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subject
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of all data being collected, processed, and stored during the registration and device enrollment process.

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: Homeowner may lack control to set preferences or provide granular consent regarding how their personal data is processed during registration.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than actually needed for account registration and device enrollment, violating GDPR data minimization principles.

title: Access code as unique identifier
description: The temporary access code serves as a unique reference to the guest's identity for this access event, allowing the system to identify which guest is attempting to access the home.

title: Observed communications during access code transmission
description: The access code transmitted from guest to home hub could be intercepted or observed by third parties during transmission.

title: Application side effect reveals access attempt
description: The system response (unlocking or denying access) reveals whether an access attempt was made, potentially exposing the guest's presence or absence.

title: Sensitive access code data collected
description: The access code is sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required for the access control functionality.

title: Potential unnecessary processing of access code
description: The home hub may analyze or store the access code beyond what is functionally needed for unlocking the door.

title: Guest unaware of access code processing
description: The guest may not be fully aware of how their access code is being processed, stored, or potentially shared by the home hub system.

title: Lack of guest control over access code preferences
description: The guest may not have control over preferences regarding how their access code is used, stored, or retained by the system.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data (access code details) than is actually needed for the simple access control functionality.

title: Quasi-identifier combining sensor event data
description: Motion, door, and sensor events can be combined to create a quasi-identifier profile of household activity patterns, potentially linking to specific individuals or households.
assumptions: Events contain timestamp and location data that can be correlated

title: Revealing attributes in sensor events
description: The type, frequency, and timing of sensor events (motion, door access) reveal attributes about household occupancy and behavior that can support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Event metadata includes timestamps and event types

title: Data type sensitivity - sensor data collection
description: Sensor event data (motion, door access) may be perceived as highly sensitive personal data, potentially collected beyond what is functionally required for basic home automation.
assumptions: Sensor data can infer presence and behavior patterns

title: Duration/retention of event data
description: Event data may be stored in the local log longer than functionally needed, creating unnecessary privacy risk through prolonged data availability.
assumptions: No explicit retention policy defined for event logs
uncertainty_note: Assuming no retention policy is in place

title: Unawareness of processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects (household members) may not be aware that their motion, door, and sensor events are being logged and stored.
assumptions: No explicit consent or notification mechanism for event logging

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding which sensor events are collected and stored in the local log.
assumptions: No user-configurable settings for event logging

title: Excessive data retention at destination
description: The local event log may retain sensor data longer than functionally needed, increasing privacy risk through prolonged data availability.
assumptions: No automatic deletion or retention policy for stored events
uncertainty_note: Assuming no retention policy is in place

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing and storing all sensor events may exceed what is actually needed for the functional goals of the home automation system.
assumptions: Full event logging may not be necessary for core functionality

title: Processing of identified data at source
description: Home Hub processes and uploads video clips that contain identified information about individuals captured by the camera, including faces, activities, and locations.

title: Data type sensitivity at source
description: Video clips are highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for the home security system's intended purpose.

title: Identifiable information in metadata during transit
description: Video files and their metadata in transit may contain identifying information about the data subject, such as timestamps, device identifiers, or location data.

title: Linking through quasi-identifiers in transit
description: Metadata accompanying video clips (timestamps, device IDs, location) can serve as quasi-identifiers that enable linking of data to specific individuals.

title: Processing of identified data at destination
description: Cloud Video Storage processes and stores video clips containing identified information about individuals, enabling identification of data subjects.

title: Excessive party exposure at destination
description: Cloud storage may make video data accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including cloud service providers, administrators, or third parties.

title: Excessive data retention at destination
description: Cloud storage may retain video clips longer than functionally needed for the home security system's purpose.

title: Lack of data subject control at destination
description: Data subjects may lack control over how their video data is processed, stored, or accessed once uploaded to cloud storage.

title: GDPR data minimization violation at destination
description: Processing and storing video data may violate GDPR data minimization principle if more personal data is processed than actually needed.

title: Linking through device/user identifiers in motion alerts
description: Motion alerts may contain device identifiers or user references that can be used to link data to specific individuals or households, enabling tracking of presence and behavior patterns.
assumptions: Assumes motion alerts include or can be correlated with user/device identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier combining through motion data
description: Motion data combined with timestamp, location, and other contextual information can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific individuals, revealing presence patterns and routines.
assumptions: Motion data includes timestamp and location context that can be combined with other data sources

title: Revealing attributes through motion detection
description: Motion alerts reveal revealing attributes such as presence/absence, time of activity, and movement patterns that can support identification of data subjects and their behaviors.
assumptions: Motion data inherently reveals behavioral patterns and presence information

title: Excessive data granularity in motion alerts
description: Real-time motion alerts may be more granular than functionally needed, capturing detailed movement information that exceeds what is required for basic security monitoring purposes.
assumptions: Full motion data is transmitted rather than aggregated or summarized data

title: High frequency of motion data processing
description: Real-time motion alerts are processed at high frequency, potentially exceeding what is functionally needed for security monitoring and alert purposes.
assumptions: Every motion event triggers an alert and data transmission

title: Unawareness of motion data collection and transmission
description: Data subjects (home occupants) may not be aware that their motion data is being collected and transmitted to external backend systems in real-time.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into data transmission processes

title: Lack of user control over motion data preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences regarding what motion data is collected, how it's processed, or when alerts are sent to the backend.
assumptions: Limited user configuration options for motion data handling

title: Data propagation to additional services
description: Mobile app backend may propagate motion data to other services or systems where it is not functionally needed, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: Backend may share data with third-party services or analytics systems

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing motion data beyond what is strictly necessary for the functional goal of security monitoring may violate data minimization requirements.
assumptions: System processes more motion data than functionally required

title: Quasi-identifier combining in aggregated analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., device type, location patterns, usage frequency) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individual users when combined with external data.
assumptions: Aggregation may not be sufficiently coarse-grained to prevent re-identification through quasi-identifier combination.
uncertainty_note: Assuming aggregation is not perfectly anonymized

title: Group profiling through aggregated data
description: The cloud analytics vendor may profile groups of individuals based on the aggregated device-usage analytics, deriving insights about group behaviors and characteristics that could be used to infer information about individual users.
assumptions: Analytics vendor has capability to perform group-level profiling from aggregated data.
uncertainty_note: Depends on vendor's analytics capabilities and intent

title: Quasi-identifiers in metadata or data fields
description: The aggregated device-usage analytics may contain quasi-identifiers (combinations of attributes) that could allow identification of data subjects when cross-referenced with other data sources.
assumptions: Data fields may contain attribute combinations that are unique or near-unique to individuals.
uncertainty_note: Depends on granularity of aggregation and data fields included

title: Excessive data granularity in analytics
description: The device-usage analytics may be disclosed at a finer granularity than functionally necessary for the analytics vendor's purposes, potentially exposing more detailed user behavior information than required.
assumptions: Analytics vendor may not need highly granular data to perform their analysis functions.
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific analytics requirements and data minimization practices

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Personal data is shared with a predetermined external party (cloud analytics vendor) beyond what may be functionally necessary, expanding the exposure of data to external entities.
assumptions: The cloud analytics vendor is a known, predetermined recipient of the data.
uncertainty_note: This is inherent to the flow design - data is explicitly shared with EE3

title: User unawareness of data sharing with third party
description: Data subjects (mobile app users) may not be fully aware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with an external cloud analytics vendor, as this may not be clearly communicated in the app's privacy policy or user interface.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into all data sharing activities with third-party vendors.
uncertainty_note: Depends on app's privacy disclosure practices

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or provide granular consent regarding how their device-usage analytics are shared with the cloud analytics vendor, potentially unable to opt-out or customize the data sharing.
assumptions: The app may not provide meaningful user controls for third-party data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Depends on app's consent and preference mechanisms

title: Data accessible to external analytics vendor beyond necessity
description: The cloud analytics vendor receives personal data that may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, as the vendor may have access to the data for purposes beyond the specific analytics engagement.
assumptions: The vendor may share or further process the data with other parties or for other purposes.
uncertainty_note: Depends on vendor's data handling practices and contractual obligations

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The processing of device-usage analytics by the cloud analytics vendor may involve processing more personal data than is actually needed for the analytics functionality, violating the data minimization principle under GDPR.
assumptions: GDPR applies to the data processing activities, and the vendor may process data beyond what's necessary.
uncertainty_note: Depends on vendor's actual data processing practices and compliance measures

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The DataStore contains video clips that are identified with specific homeowners/users. When retrieving video for playback, the system processes identified personal data tied to individual data subjects.

title: Video data contains unique user identifiers
description: Stored video clips are associated with specific homeowner accounts through unique identifiers, enabling identification of the data subject from the video data.

title: Linking through video metadata identifiers
description: Video data in transit may contain metadata (timestamps, device IDs, user IDs) that can be used to link the video content to specific individuals or their activities.

title: Video data type sensitivity
description: Video content is inherently sensitive personal data that captures visual information about individuals, their activities, and potentially their environment, which may be more sensitive than functionally required for simple playback.

title: Video data propagation risk
description: Video data retrieved for playback may be accessible to or propagated to other services beyond the immediate playback functionality, increasing exposure risk.

title: Excessive video granularity
description: The Mobile App Backend may process video data at a finer granularity than needed for playback, potentially extracting or analyzing more detail than functionally required.

title: Homeowner unawareness of video retrieval
description: The homeowner (data subject) may not be aware when their stored video clips are being accessed or retrieved by the backend system for playback.

title: Limited homeowner control over video processing
description: Homeowners may lack control over how their video data is processed, stored, or shared by the Mobile App Backend beyond basic playback functionality.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing video data for playback may involve collecting and processing more personal data than strictly necessary for the functional goal of video playback.
